News and media releases

Media releases and other news items published by the CAA.

You can sign up to receive media releases by email, as well as notifications about other topics, through our email notification service. If you're looking for what's recently been published on the CAA website, see our What's new page.

Drone operator sentenced for serious aviation safety breaches

15 Jul 2026

A Napier man has been sentenced to 150 hours of community work after being found guilty of four charges relating to unsafe drone flights in controlled airspace near Napier Airport.

CAA transitions Dangerous Goods training delivery to industry

13 Jul 2026

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has concluded its interim delivery of Dangerous Goods (DG) training for small aeroplane and helicopter operators, with responsibility for training delivery transitioning fully to industry.

Updates to security screening at Hamilton Airport

8 Jul 2026

From 15 July 2026, passengers travelling through Hamilton Airport will notice a change to our security screening process.

CAA sets direction and priorities with latest planning documents including new 2026-2027 safety and security focus areas

2 Jul 2026

The Civil Aviation Authority’s (CAA) Statement of Intent (SOI) and Statement of Performance Expectations (SPE), published on 1 July, set out what the organisation will deliver and how it will measure progress.

Changes to security screening at Invercargill Airport

17 Jun 2026

From 29 June 2026, passengers travelling through Invercargill Airport will notice a change to our security screening process.

Minister visits CAA staff to recognise progress improving aviation services and safety oversight

16 Jun 2026

Acting Minister of Transport with responsibility for Aviation, Hon James Meager, has visited Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) staff to recognise the work of the Aviation Safety Oversight Group and the progress made over the past year to strengthen aviation safety and improve services for the sector.

CAA addresses recent media coverage – 9 June 2026

9 Jun 2026

Following recent reporting by Michael Morrah at The New Zealand Herald about employment related matters, Civil Aviation Authority Board Chair Mark Darrow has provided a statement.

Civil Aviation rules update work launched

29 Apr 2026

Acting Minister of Transport James Meager has announced details of the Civil Aviation Authority’s (CAA) rules update programme which aims to modernise New Zealand’s civil aviation rules, increase alignment with international standards, and be more responsive to the aviation sector’s needs.

CAA appoints new Chief Digital Officer

20 Apr 2026

After a thorough recruitment process, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is pleased to announce the appointment of Aaron Toatelegese as Chief Digital Officer to its Executive Leadership Team.

Easter Bunny and CAA share egg-spert tips to pack smart

27 Mar 2026

With more than 6,500 power banks, hair straighteners and curling irons removed from checked bags so far this year, the Civil Aviation Authority is urging passengers to check the rules before flying these school holidays.

CAA appoints new Chief Financial Officer

20 Mar 2026

After a thorough recruitment process, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is pleased to announce the appointment of Brett Banner as Chief Financial Officer to its Executive Leadership Team.

CAA appoints new Deputy Chief Executive – Gayle Holmes

12 Feb 2026

After a thorough recruitment process, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is pleased to announce the appointment of Gayle Holmes as our new Deputy Chief Executive, Regulatory Enablement and Response, to the Executive Leadership Team.

ICAO Audit confirms New Zealand’s sound aviation safety system

15 Jan 2026

The Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA) welcomes the findings of the 2025 International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Universal Safety Oversight Audit Programme (USOAP), which confirm that New Zealand has a sound and effective aviation safety system, with no significant safety issues identified.

Updated Civil Aviation Rules for drones and advanced aviation now in effect

22 Dec 2025

A package of modernised Civil Aviation Rules for drones and advanced aviation takes effect today, providing clearer expectations for operators and supporting safe technology development across New Zealand.

CAA urges travellers to carry power banks and spare lithium batteries with them

9 Dec 2025

Travellers are being reminded that spare lithium batteries must be correctly packed in carry-on only.

CAA statement on Airbus A320 software issue

29 Nov 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is aware of the Airbus A320 situation and is working closely with Air New Zealand (and other relevant agencies) in response to an emergency airworthiness directive from the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), requiring A320s to have a software update.

Clearer rules and a new pathway to support innovation in NZ’s skies

27 Nov 2025

Updated drone and advanced aviation rules will take effect on 22 December 2025, introducing a new Part 107 to support research and development flight testing, and providing greater clarity for drone operators.

CAA invites aviation sector to help shape the future of NZ’s aviation rules

10 Nov 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA) will shortly begin a prioritised work programme to update the Civil Aviation Rules — an important step in keeping New Zealand’s aviation system safe, efficient, and fit for the future.

CAA approves electric aircraft for demonstration flights in NZ

6 Nov 2025

The shift towards electric aircraft is no longer a distant idea, it’s here and reshaping how we think about regulation and innovation in aviation.

CAA announces new Board Deputy Chair

22 Oct 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) Board Chair, Mark Darrow, has welcomed the appointment of Mike Schubert as Deputy Chair of the CAA Board. 

CAA welcomes three new Board members

24 Sept 2025

The Associate Minister of Transport, James Meager, today announced three new Civil Aviation Authority Board members.

Don McCracken receives Civil Aviation Authority Director’s Award

16 Sept 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority has presented Don McCracken with the 2025 Director’s Award at the Aviation Industry Awards Gala Dinner in Wellington.

Unlicensed helicopter flights lead to conviction

12 Sept 2025

A helicopter pilot has been convicted for flying without a license or certificate and obstruction.

CAA to start funding review this year

28 Aug 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA) is commencing a first principles review of how we are funded, with a goal to ensure New Zealand’s aviation safety and security system remains sustainable, fair, and fit for purpose into the future.

Unqualified pilot sentenced for dangerous and unlawful flying

25 Jul 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) welcomes the sentencing of a man who was fined $14,475 for multiple serious breaches of aviation safety rules, including flying without a pilot licence, flying an aircraft without a certificate of airworthiness, and operating in a manner that caused unnecessary danger.

New Zealand welcomes aviation system safety audit

3 Jul 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA) welcomes auditors from the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) who will undertake a full safety audit of New Zealand’s aviation system from 9 – 22 July 2025.

Civil Aviation Authority signs contract with Airways International to deliver Aeronautical Information Services

30 Jun 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is pleased to sign a new contract with Airways International Limited (AIL) for the provision of Aeronautical Information Services (AIS) in New Zealand.

Special Use Airspace creates more flexibility for advanced aviation research and development

27 Jun 2025

Research and development for advanced aviation will take another step forward in New Zealand when a permanent Special Use Airspace approval comes into effect on 7 August 2025.

CAA Board announce successor for Director of Civil Aviation and Chief Executive role

18 Jun 2025

With the pending retirement of Keith Manch at the end of this year, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) Board is pleased to announce the appointment of the next Director of Civil Aviation and Chief Executive.

New Zealand collaborates with international aviation regulators on roadmap for aircraft of the future

17 Jun 2025

Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) aircraft are set to be certified in a unified and streamlined way across the world following a landmark Roadmap established between national aviation authorities from Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

Unreported hard landing likely contributed to fatal glider crash

17 Jun 2025

Following a fatal glider accident in February 2024, the Civil Aviation Authority has released its investigation report, highlighting three key safety takeaways for the aviation community.

CAA Act 2023 and a new structure in place

13 Jun 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is making changes on how we work to improve our performance as New Zealand’s safety and security regulator.

CAA appoints two new Deputy Chief Executives – Catherine MacGowan & Fred Stein

6 Jun 2025

After a thorough international search, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is pleased to announce the appointment of two new Deputy Chief Executives to our Executive Leadership Team.

Jill Hatchwell and Terry Murdoch retire from CAA Board

6 May 2025

After serving two full terms with the Civil Aviation Authority’s Board, Jill Hatchwell’s term will end on 31 July 2025. Terry Murdoch, who joined as part of the new Board appointments in August 2024, has retired due to health reasons.

New Zealand’s State Safety Programme has been updated

1 May 2025

We’re pleased to publish the 2025 edition of New Zealand’s State Safety Programme (SSP).

Civil Aviation Authority New Zealand seeks industry feedback on Asia-Pacific Reference Materials to facilitate operations of Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Advanced Air Mobility

11 Apr 2025

The Reference Materials, jointly developed by 24 Asia-Pacific States and Administrations, will help reduce regulatory cost and risk to investments, support industry development and accelerate safe adoption.

Civil Aviation Act 2023 coming into effect next week

3 Apr 2025

It is just a couple of days till 5 April when the Civil Aviation Act 2023 (CA Act 2023) comes into effect.

Fly More, Fly Smart: CAA urges pilots not to ‘wing it’

10 Mar 2025

The thrill of free flight is unparalleled—the wind, the lift, the pure freedom. But even the most experienced pilots know that every flight demands smart decision-making. Following a recent rise in hang gliding, paragliding, and speed wing incidents—including a recent speed wing fatality—the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is urging pilots to sharpen their situational awareness and decision-making before, during, and after each flight.

Safety in New Zealand’s aviation system to be audited this year

26 Feb 2025

The International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) will conduct a safety audit of New Zealand’s aviation system in July 2025. The audit looks at the government agencies responsible for setting and administering policy, rules regulations; as well as operators and participants within the aviation system responsible for complying with rules and regulations and upholding aviation safety.

Investigations information brochure

25 Feb 2025

In relation to our recent changes to CAA investigation practices we’ve published a brochure which outlines our approach to investigating aviation accidents, occurrences, and compliance with rules and legislation.

CAA safety campaign wraps up, but its message remains clear

13 Feb 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority has concluded its largest nationwide safety campaign, Work Together, Stay Apart (WTSA).

Recent drone usage raises serious concerns

4 Feb 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is concerned about any reports of unsafe drone operations near Auckland Airport which have the potential to delay flights.

Civil Aviation Authority confirms new structure

3 Feb 2025

Following extensive consultation with our people, the Civil Aviation Authority has confirmed changes to its structure, systems, and practices.  

Civil Aviation Authority confirms increases to levies, fees and charges

17 Jan 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority has announced increases to its levies, fees and charges, following a decision by Cabinet on 18 December 2024.

CAA releases passenger and stakeholder research results for 2024

17 Jan 2025

CAA conducts periodic research to measure public perceptions of aviation safety and security and the aviation sector views on our performance. The 2024 results are available below.

Passenger safety briefings draft Advisory Circular released for consultation

13 Jan 2025

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has drafted an Advisory Circular about cabin safety, and is seeking feedback from Deaf and disabled people, in addition to feedback from air operators and other aviation participants.

Don't let your Christmas drone cause trouble in the sky

18 Dec 2024

The Civil Aviation Authority is preparing for another season of increased complaints about new drone owners being unaware of the rules and causing problems for other people and aircraft. National data shows that reports about drone behaviour surge by 30 percent at the start of each new year.

Safe and secure travels this holiday season

17 Dec 2024

Summer is here, which means it’s the season of barbeques, parties, and events. Aviation Security Officers want you to know which well-intended gifts and items won’t make it through the security screening, so you don’t turn up empty handed at your in-law’s house.

CAA teams win special recognition award

7 Nov 2024

Four members of the Civil Aviation Authority’s safety education and certification teams won this year’s Royal Aeronautical Society’s special recognition award at the 38th annual symposium.

Civil Aviation Authority change proposal

25 Oct 2024

Statement from the Director of Civil Aviation and Chief Executive Keith Manch about a Civil Aviation Authority change proposal which includes changes to our systems, practices and structure.
